title: Accessibility
body:
**Accessibility**, frequently written a11y, is design that works for users with disabilities.
The course treats it as a requirement of a correct interface.

The practical requirements are specific and testable:

```
text alternatives     every image carries alt text, so a screen reader can
                      describe it and the meaning survives when it fails to load
colour is not alone   meaning is never carried by colour by itself, since
                      roughly one man in twelve cannot distinguish red from green
keyboard access       everything reachable by mouse is reachable by keyboard,
                      in a sensible order, with a visible focus indicator
contrast              text meets a measured contrast ratio against its background
structure             headings are real headings, so the document can be navigated
                      by structure, with no linear read needed
captions              audio content carries a text equivalent
```

Each is checkable, which is what separates accessibility from a matter of intention. An
automated tool catches contrast and missing alt text, and keyboard access is verified by
putting the mouse away and completing a task.

The general argument is that accessible design improves the product for everyone. Captions
serve a noisy room, keyboard access serves an expert who never touches the mouse, and high
contrast serves a phone screen in sunlight. Designing for the constrained case produces a
better result in the ordinary case, which is why the requirement pays for itself.

In [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]] the mechanisms are in the markup, since semantic
[[HTML]] with a real [[Form Tag]] and labelled [[Input Tag|inputs]] is accessible by
default and a div styled to look like a button is not.
